detect_tables_phase.human:
You are at step 1. of the schema integration process. You are given a source table and your task is to identify the entity types present in the table and split the table if needed based on the types found.

[DEMONSTRATION]


<sourcetable>

[TABLE_INPUT]

</sourcetable>

<instruction>
 Your instructions are the following:
1. Identify the entity types described by the table.
2. Choose one main entity type that the table primarily describes.
3. Identify any other entity types that relate to the main entity.
4. For the main entity and each related entity, list the attributes (columns) that belong to it.
5. Split the table into multiple tables ONLY if there is low overlap between attribute groups.
6. This is not database normalization.
7. Do not split out an entity if it only has a single attribute related to it.
Return the schemata of all resulting output tables in the following JSON format {"<table_name>": {"attributes": ["<attribute1>", "<attribute2>", "..."]}}
Be brief in the naming of the output table and use general terms without parenthesis.
Use the original attribute names of the source table in the output tables.
Make sure that you do not generate tables with less than three attributes.
</instruction>Reply with the correct JSON format: The JSON must follow this exact schema: {"<table_name>": {"attributes": ["<attribute1>", "<attribute2>", "..."]}} Example: {"employee": {"attributes": ["employee_id", "employee_name", "employee_age"]}, "department": {"attributes": ["department_id", "department_name"]}}.

grouping_phase.system: You are a data engineer tasked to design an integrated schema that will be used to represent all data from a set of source tables.
grouping_phase.human:
You are at step 2 of the schema integration process and are given the set of tables that results from step 1. Your task is to group (cluster) the tables that describe the same entity type, so that all tables that describe the same or semantically similar entity types are put into the same group. Name each group according to the entity type of the grouped tables. If a hierarchy can be observed between the found groups, combine the tables that are connected through this hierarchy and name the overall group after the highest entity type in the hierarchy.

<instruction>Please group (cluster) the set of tables tables by entity type, so that all tables that describe the same or similar entity types are put into the same group. Return the names of the groups together with the names of the tables in each group strictly using the following JSON format {group_name: [names of tables in the group]} with no additional commentary.
Be brief in the naming of the groups and use general terms without parenthesis.

The column headers overlap between the tables can also be used as a signal to help with the grouping.

schema_integration_phase.human:

Two columns match if they describe the same semantic concept. Afterwards, using these found matches, merge (integrate) the attributes and avoid adding to the final schema redundant attributes i.e. don't include two attributes of the same matching group in the final schema.

<instruction>

Make sure that each attribute appears only once in the integrated schema.
Do not add the table names in the column name mappings.
</instruction> Return the correct JSON format.

final_integration_phase.system: You are a data engineer tasked to design an integrated schema that will be used to represent all data from a set of source tables.
final_integration_phase.human:
You are at the end of the schema integration process. You are given a set of integrated schemas from step 3.
Examine the table schemata and the given relationships that exist between the schemata. This phase has two tasks: create identifiers for the tables IF needed (e.g. when more than one table schema is given) and remove redundant attributes, such as the same attribute appearing in the different tables. Remove redundant tables as well, e.g. if two tables can be merged together. When introducing identifiers, if there is a relationship between two table schemas (or more) use the identifiers as foreign keys and replace the old attributes.
